log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought:
Lead: 52% BRING: dragapult, 36% BRING: garchomp, 5% BRING: gholdengo
Pick 2: 70% BRING: garchomp, 23% BRING: gholdengo, 3% BRING: greninja
Pick 3: 86% BRING: gholdengo, 7% BRING: scizor, 6% BRING: greninja

Incineroar leads for Intimidate, Fake Out, and Parting Shot against their physical threats like Garchomp and Scizor. Archaludon's Dracometeor and Electroshot hit the Dragon-types hard. Kingambit adds a strong Dark/Steel physical attacker that can pressure Greninja and Gholdengo.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Looking at team preview, I'm sizing up matchups: Incineroar brings intimidate and utility with Fake Out and Parting Shot, while Kingambit's Dark/Steel typing resists Ghost and Dragon, giving it good coverage against Dragapult but leaving it exposed to Fighting, Fire, and Ground attacks.

Archaludon's Steel/Dragon typing could punish Dragapult and Garchomp with strong special attacks like Electro Shot or Draco Meteor, though it's vulnerable to Fire and Ground. I'm leaning toward leading Incineroar with Kingambit and either Archaludon or Gholdengo, weighing Gholdengo's strength against Scizor and Garchomp versus Archaludon's raw power against the opposing Dragons.

decisions.thought: 33% MOVE: suckerpunch, 25% SWITCH: garchomp, 17% MOVE: shadowball

Fake Out does nothing to Dragapult because Ghost is immune to Normal, and Flare Blitz is resisted by Dragon. Parting Shot lowers Dragapult's Attack and Sp. Atk while pivoting Incineroar out safely. That sets up Kingambit or Archaludon to take the next turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Fake Out won't work since Dragapult's Ghost typing blocks Normal moves entirely, and Flare Blitz is resisted by Dragon. Protect seems wasteful here, so I'm considering Parting Shot to debuff Dragapult's attacking stats while pivoting out to a better matchup.

Bringing in Kingambit seems promising since its Dark typing resists Ghost-type attacks, making it a safer switch-in against Dragapult's Ghost moves, while Dragon-type attacks hit it neutrally.

So I'll go with Parting Shot here to weaken Dragapult's offenses and pivot into Kingambit, which can threaten back with Kowtow Cleave despite being slower.

decisions.thought: Incineroar must leave, and Dragapult is at -2 Attack, which weakens its Sucker Punch. Kingambit resists Dark-type attacks and hits Dragapult's Ghost typing with super-effective Dark moves, so it is the better switch-in.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Incineroar at 202 HP I need to switch out, choosing between Archaludon and Kingambit. Checking Dragapult's typing against Archaludon's Steel/Dragon—Steel resists Dragon, so that matchup looks safer than I first thought.

Comparing against Kingambit: its Dark/Steel typing resists Sucker Punch well, and its own Dark-type moves like Kowtow Cleave hit Dragapult's Ghost typing super effectively. With Dragapult's attack already lowered, Kingambit seems like the stronger switch-in here.

decisions.thought: 62% MOVE: suckerpunch, 29% SWITCH: garchomp, 8% SWITCH: gholdengo

Dragapult is faster, but its Attack is at -2, so its Sucker Punch can't threaten a 177 HP Kingambit. Kowtow Cleave is a super-effective Dark STAB move boosted by Black Glasses, and it doesn't miss, so it should KO or nearly KO Dragapult this turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm weighing Kingambit against Dragapult: Dragapult's stats are lowered, but it's faster and its Dark-type Sucker Punch could matter, while Kingambit's Dark STAB move hits Dragapult's Ghost typing super effectively.

I'm calculating Kowtow Cleave's damage output, factoring in STAB, item boost, and the type advantage against Dragapult's defense and estimated HP range to see if it's close to a KO this turn.

Dragapult's sucker punch at -2 attack would be weak and unlikely to KO Kingambit first, so Kowtow Cleave looks like the right call, especially since Dark is super effective against the Ghost typing with Dragon being neutral. I'll go with kowtowcleave.

decisions.thought: 83% MOVE: earthquake, 5% MOVE: swordsdance, 5% SWITCH: gholdengo

Garchomp is faster than Kingambit, so it will hit first, but Earthquake is only neutral-to-Kingambit's typing with Steel taking 2x, and Kingambit has 168 HP to absorb it. Swords Dance risks a big hit for no immediate KO. Kowtow Cleave is a boosted, never-miss Dark attack that does solid damage now.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking Kingambit's attack types against Garchomp's Dragon/Ground typing—Dark Pulse and Iron Head both land neutral against that combination, so no crucial type advantage either way there.

The real danger is speed and Earthquake: Garchomp outspeeds Kingambit and its Ground-type moves hit Kingambit's Steel typing for double damage, likely dealing 60-80% against Kingambit's 168 HP, while Garchomp's Dragon moves are only resisted by half against Dark/Steel. Kowtow Cleave never misses and with Black Glasses plus a Supreme Overlord boost could still deal solid damage, but Kingambit risks a major hit before it can act if it tries to set up Swords Dance.

Switching to Incineroar doesn't help much since Ground is neutral against Fire/Dark and Fire is resisted by Dragon anyway. I'll just go with Kowtow Cleave since it's guaranteed to connect and still hits reasonably hard.

decisions.thought: Kingambit has fainted, so I must switch. Garchomp's Earthquake is super effective on Archaludon (Steel weakness), which would be a bad trade. Incineroar takes Earthquake neutrally and its Intimidate on entry cuts Garchomp's Attack.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: With Kingambit fainted, I need to pick between Archaludon and Incineroar against Garchomp's Earthquake. Archaludon's Steel typing takes double damage from Ground, while Incineroar is Fire/Dark and takes Earthquake neutrally, making it the safer switch-in.

decisions.thought: 78% MOVE: earthquake, 8% MOVE: swordsdance, 6% SWITCH: gholdengo

Fake Out is illegal because Incineroar has already been on the field, and Flare Blitz is resisted by Garchomp's Dragon typing. Parting Shot drops Garchomp's Attack to -2 and brings in Archaludon, whose Dracometeor hits Garchomp super effectively. That is the best setup.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Incineroar out and Garchomp at 90% with Atk already lowered, Fake Out won't work since it's past the first turn on field. Flare Blitz only does half damage to Garchomp due to its Dragon typing, but Garchomp outspeeds anyway. I'm checking if Earthquake threatens Incineroar - it's Fire/Dark so Ground hits neutrally.

Switching to Archaludon seems risky since its Steel typing takes double damage from Earthquake despite decent bulk. Parting Shot could drop Garchomp's offenses further before bringing in Archaludon, though that still leaves it exposed to a 2x EQ hit. Protect might just stall while taking recoil from Life Orb, so I'm leaning toward estimating Flare Blitz's resisted damage output against Garchomp's defense stats to see if trading hits is viable.

decisions.thought: Only one legal action is available: switching to Archaludon. Incineroar has fainted, so this is a forced replacement and I should submit it.
67% MOVE: earthquake, 12% MOVE: dracometeor, 8% MOVE: swordsdance

Garchomp is Dragon/Ground, so Electroshot does nothing. Dracometeor is a super-effective STAB hit from Archaludon's 194 Sp. Atk and is the strongest option. Garchomp is faster and threatens big Earthquake damage, so I'm taking the highest-damage play now rather than protecting.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Garchomp is sitting at 80% HP, somewhere in the 146-172 range depending on its actual max. Archaludon's Dragon Meteor would hit super effectively here since Archaludon is Steel/Dragon with 194 special attack, giving it STAB against Garchomp's 94-150 special defense range.

Electroshot does nothing since Garchomp is part Ground-type. Flash Cannon is only neutral damage, so Dracometeor is clearly the strongest option despite its accuracy drawback. Garchomp will likely move first with Earthquake, and Steel-types take double damage from Ground moves, so Archaludon needs to make this hit count. I'm going with Dracometeor.

decisions.thought: 86% MOVE: shadowball, 8% MOVE: recover, 3% MOVE: flashcannon

Archaludon is at 62 HP with Sp. Atk at -2, so its damage is weak and Gholdengo can likely OHKO it. Electroshot is neutral on Gholdengo, hits for 130, and raises Sp. Atk by 1 to recover some damage output. Protect only delays the problem, and Dracometeor would lower Sp. Atk again.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Archaludon down to 62 HP and SpA dropped two stages, I'm checking type matchups against Gholdengo's Steel/Ghost typing to see if Electric is resisted.

Actually Steel doesn't resist Electric, so Electroshot would land neutral but Dracometeor and Flash Cannon would be weakened by Gholdengo's Steel resistance. The bigger worry is Gholdengo's bulk and Shadow Ball or Make It Rain potentially finishing off Archaludon given its already low HP.

Weighing the options, since Archaludon lacks recovery and Protect only stalls, I'd lean toward Electroshot since it raises SpA and could hit hard if Archaludon moves first.
